newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower, pressured by JGB fall.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower, pressured by JGB fall.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen futures settled lower on Tuesday after coming under downward pressure from sharp sales of Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, but traders said further falls were unlikely.
Key June JGB futures slipped after options-linked sales and poor results from a four-year note auction.
The December Euroyen futures contract ended at 98.85 after moving from 98.84 to 98.90. Turnover was 92,483 contracts.
"The market was led today mainly by the moves in JGBs, with virtually no fresh factors in the Euroyen futures market itself," one city bank trader said.

JGB traders said the sharp fall in the key June 10-year bond futures may have been triggered by sales from hedge funds, said to be holding a large number of June JGB put options with a strike price of 123.00.

Although the key December Euroyen contract went as low as 98.84 at one point, it then appeared to recover slightly on short-covering, a trader with a securities firm said, adding that slides below 98.81 in the short term seem unlikely.

He added, and the city bank trader agreed, that the key December is likely to move roughly in a 98.85-98.95 range over the next few days. "Rises much beyond this are unlikely for now, as the impact of Sakakibara's comments last week still lingers, keeping the topside heavy," he said.
Senior MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted as saying last week that a rise in Japan's discount rate should be expected in the coming year.
A trust bank dealer said the market will be reluctant to move aggressively until the release of April industrial production figures on Thursday.

In the interbank market, key overnight call money was traded at around 0.52 percent, up from Monday's 0.51 percent. Traders said this appeared to be due to increasing funds demand ahead of the month-end.
Around 200 billion worth of long end benchmark three month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.60 percent, highest since March 25 and up from 0.58 percent Friday.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected 600 billion yen into the money market in its regular morning operation, against a projected 600 billion yen shortfall. The operation was in line with market expectations. --E. Lies +81-3-3432-8806
